title: Two friends over a few months

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Have you had a chance to look at that flat listing I sent?

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: I did. The kitchen is tiny but the light is unreal. Which floor is it on?

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Third, no lift. That is the bit I keep going back and forth on.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Three flights with shopping every week adds up. How long is the commute?

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Twenty five minutes door to door, which is half what I do now.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Then the stairs are worth it. You would get back nearly an hour a day.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: That is roughly how I have been thinking about it too.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: What is the rent compared to your current place?

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Ninety pounds more a month. Not nothing, but not the deal breaker.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Does that include bills?

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Water and building maintenance, not heating or electricity.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Ask what the heating bill ran to last winter. A top floor flat with old windows can be brutal.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Good shout. I will email the agent tonight.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Also ask if the boiler was serviced this year. They have to have a certificate.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Agent says the boiler was replaced in January and the windows were done two years ago.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: That is better than I expected. Then I think you take it.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: I put the holding deposit down this morning.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Congratulations. When do you move?

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Fourteenth. Which gives me three weeks to get rid of half my things.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: I can come and help on the Saturday if that is useful.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: It really would be. I will feed you.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Sold.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: How did the interview go?

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Better than I thought. Two hours, three people, and they actually let me finish sentences.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Low bar but a real one. What did they ask?

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: A lot about the reporting project. They wanted to know what I would do differently.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: What did you say?

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: That I would have talked to the people using it before building anything, instead of after.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: That is a good answer because it is true.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: They seemed to like it. There is a third round though.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: What is in it?

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: A presentation to the wider team. Forty minutes on how I would approach their data problem.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Do you have enough about their data problem to build forty minutes?

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Not really. They sent a two page brief and it is mostly marketing language.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Then ask for a call with whoever owns the problem. If they say no, that tells you something too.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: I asked and they said yes. Half an hour on Thursday with the head of analytics.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: That is a good sign. They want you to do well.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: The call was useful. Their actual issue is that nobody trusts the numbers, not that the numbers are wrong.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: That is a completely different talk to the one the brief implied.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Which is why it was worth asking. I am rewriting the whole thing tonight.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: How did the presentation land?

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: They asked questions for twenty minutes afterwards, which I am taking as a good sign.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: It usually is. Silence is the bad one.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: I got the offer this morning.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: That is brilliant. Are you taking it?

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: I think so. It is a small pay rise but the work is much closer to what I want to do.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: How is the notice period?

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: A month. So I finish at the end of next month and start in the middle of the one after.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Take the two weeks in between and go somewhere.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: That is exactly what I was thinking.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: So, somewhere for two weeks. Any ideas?

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Depends what you want. Doing nothing, or walking eight hours a day?

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Somewhere in between. Warm, walkable, not too expensive.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Portugal. Fly into Porto, work your way down the coast.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: How long would that take?

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: You could do Porto, Coimbra and Lisbon comfortably in ten days with trains between them.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Are the trains any good?

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Very. Porto to Lisbon is under three hours and it is a nice ride.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: What is Coimbra like?

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Old university town, hilly, quieter than the other two. Worth two nights, not more.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: And what would I actually do in Porto?

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Walk the river, eat too much, take the tram to the coast at Foz.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: What time of year is best?

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Late September or early October. Still warm, far fewer people, and the prices drop.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: That fits perfectly with the gap between jobs.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Then book the flights before you talk yourself out of it.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Booked. Porto on the twenty ninth, back from Lisbon on the eleventh.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Where are you staying?

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Small place in Cedofeita for the first four nights. It looked less polished than the ones in the centre.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Good instinct. The centre is lovely and completely full of people like us.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Anything I should book ahead?

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Nothing much, but the good restaurants fill up. Book the ones you actually care about a week out.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Any you would send me to?

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: There is a tiny place near the market that does one fish dish a day and nothing else. I will dig out the name.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Please do.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: My knee has been sore since the run on Sunday.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Sore where exactly? Front, side, behind?

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Outside, just above the joint. It gets worse going downhill.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: That sounds like the IT band rather than the knee itself.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: How do you tell the difference?

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: IT band pain is usually a sharp line on the outside and it hates downhills specifically. Knee problems hurt going up as well.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Then it is that, because uphill is completely fine.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: How much did you increase your mileage?

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: From about fifteen to twenty five a week. Over maybe three weeks.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: There it is. That is a two thirds jump and the usual advice is ten percent a week.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: So I need to stop?

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Not stop, but back off to fifteen and stay off the hills for a fortnight.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Will it heal on its own?

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Usually, if you take the load off early. If you push through it, it takes months instead of weeks.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Anything else worth doing?

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Hip and glute work. It is almost always weakness there rather than a problem at the knee.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: That is not what I expected.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: It surprises everyone. The knee is where it hurts, not where it is caused.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Two weeks easy and it is basically gone.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Good. Now build back slowly, and add the hills last rather than first.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Did you ever sort the car?

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Not yet. It still makes that noise when I turn right at low speed.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Describe the noise.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: A dry clicking, roughly in time with the wheels.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Only on right turns or on both?

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Much worse on right, and only when the wheel is near full lock.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: That is a CV joint, most likely the left hand one.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Is that expensive?

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: The part is cheap. The labour is a few hours. Two hundred and fifty to four hundred depending on the garage.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Is it safe to drive in the meantime?

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: For short distances at low speed, yes. Do not take it on a long motorway run.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: What happens if I ignore it?

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: It eventually fails, and if it fails while turning you lose drive to that wheel with no warning.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: That settles it. Booking it in.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Get a second quote. The first garage I called quoted almost double the second for the same job.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Three hundred and ten, done Thursday. Second quote was four hundred and sixty.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Worth the phone call then.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: It is completely silent now. I had stopped noticing how loud it was.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: That is how it goes. It gets worse slowly enough that you adjust.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: What are you reading at the moment?

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: A long novel about a family running a hotel over about fifty years. Slow but I cannot put it down.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Is it depressing?

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Sad in places but not bleak. More that time passes and people miss each other.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: That is my kind of thing. Send me the title.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Will do. What did you finish last?

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: That book about the deep sea. Half of it is genuinely alarming.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Alarming how?

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Mostly how little of it anyone has actually looked at. We have better maps of Mars.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Have you seen anything worth watching?

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: There is a documentary about a bridge collapse that is far better than it sounds.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Sell it to me.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: It is really about how nobody wanted to be the person who said stop.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Now I want to watch it.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: It is about ninety minutes and it does not waste any of them.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Are you doing anything for your birthday?

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: I was going to ignore it, but the new job starts that week so maybe not.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Do something small. You have had a big couple of months.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Maybe dinner. Eight people, somewhere we can actually hear each other.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Then not that place with the tiled floors. Nobody heard anything last time.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Agreed. Somewhere with soft furnishings and a table for eight.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: The Italian near the park has a back room. I think it seats about ten.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Do they take bookings that size?

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: They do, but a couple of weeks ahead for a weekend.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Booked for the Saturday. Back room, eight of us, eight o'clock.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Perfect. Do you want anything or is presence enough?

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Presence is enough. I am about to move flat, I do not need more objects.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Very sensible and I will ignore it completely.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Thought you might.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: How was it in the end?

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Genuinely lovely. Everyone stayed until midnight and the back room was the right call.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Good. You looked like you needed a night that was not about logistics.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: I did. Thank you for pushing me into it.
